findings.title: Gate cap.vocab_arm_honest reports 'armed, did not fire' instead of UNREACHABLE when CAP_TARGETS=off -- the shipped default -- collapsing the exact three-state distinction spine/gate.py exists to preserve, on every stock run of this tree
findings.failure: Completely default configuration (CAP_TARGETS defaults to "off" -- capacity/levers.py:180 -- and LM_MASK_DEAD_ROWS defaults to False -- lm/levers.py:461). Calling capacity.api.new_valve(cfg) and printing valve.gates[1].line() prints 'Gate cap.vocab_arm_honest: armed, did not fire (False vs True)' -- a REACHABLE, unfired reading -- even though CAP_TARGETS=off means no vocabulary lift can EVER happen this run, on any configuration of LM_MASK_DEAD_ROWS. The sibling Gate two lines above, cap.valve, evaluates the identical condition (targets=="off") correctly and reports 'UNREACHABLE (off vs off) -- CAP_TARGETS=off: both caps sit at their hard ceilings and no lift can happen. Reported unreachable rather than as 0 lifts, which would read as a valve that ran and never fired -- the exact confusion this mechanism's own history is.' cap.vocab_arm_honest asks a strictly narrower question ('if a vocabulary lift could happen, would it be honest') that is equally inapplicable when targets=="off", yet the ternary at lines 176-182 routes targets=="off" into the REACHABLE branch whenever mask_dead is False, instead of into the reachable=False branch the way cap.valve does. A report reading this Gate on the shipped default sees a mechanism that 'ran and did not meet its condition' -- an operator who then sets LM_MASK_DEAD_ROWS=1 believing they closed a real gap has changed nothing observable, because the valve was never going to touch the vocabulary either way.
findings.evidence: src/capacity/api.py:176-182: `Gate("cap.vocab_arm_honest", mask_dead, mask_dead, True) if mask_dead or targets == "off" else Gate("cap.vocab_arm_honest", False, False, True, reachable=False, reason="LM_MASK_DEAD_ROWS=0: ...")`. Because Gate.reachable defaults to True (spine/gate.py:41), the condition `mask_dead or targets == "off"` sends BOTH `mask_dead=True` (genuinely honest, correctly reachable) and `mask_dead=False and targets=="off"` (nothing to be honest ABOUT, should be unreachable) into the same reachable=True branch, differing only in the `fired` value they carry (True vs False) -- so the off-valve case prints as a live, unmet condition rather than as inapplicable. Reproduced live: `python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'src'); from spine import assemble, lever, rng; lever._reopen_assembly(); rng.reset_issued(); configs,_,_=assemble.build(environ={'DATA_AREAS':'eng','CAP_TARGETS':'off','LM_MASK_DEAD_ROWS':'0'}); from capacity import api as cap_api; v=cap_api.new_valve(configs['CAP']); print([g.line() for g in v.gates])"` printed `['Gate cap.valve: UNREACHABLE (off vs off) -- CAP_TARGETS=off: ...', 'Gate cap.vocab_arm_honest: armed, did not fire (False vs True)']` -- the two Gates evaluating the SAME condition (targets=="off") and reaching opposite reachability verdicts. capacity/api.py had zero findings filed against it in either audit round (grep across p4_round1_findings.json and every r2_hunt_*.json/r2_triage_*.json/r2_sweep.json for "capacity" or "src/capacity" returns nothing), and there is no capacity.json in .rework/audits/todo/ -- the whole package was never on anyone's work list.
findings.fix: Route targets=="off" to the reachable=False branch explicitly and independently of mask_dead, the way cap.valve already does two lines above: `if targets == "off": Gate("cap.vocab_arm_honest", False, mask_dead, True, reachable=False, reason="CAP_TARGETS=off: no vocabulary lift can ever happen, so whether dead rows are masked cannot make one dishonest.") elif mask_dead: Gate("cap.vocab_arm_honest", True, True, True) else: Gate("cap.vocab_arm_honest", False, False, True, reachable=False, reason="LM_MASK_DEAD_ROWS=0: ...")` -- a three-way branch instead of the current two-way one that conflates 'honest' with 'inapplicable'.

coverage: AST-enumerated every non-stub (no NotImplementedError-raising body) top-level function in src/*/api.py -- capacity(1: new_valve), ckpt(4: saving_on, save_period, resume_source, load), data(7: _holdout_key, open_areas, _read_area, _holdout_overlap, _synthetic_areas, data_plan, draw_stream), domains(4: __init__, _live, open_partition, manage_period), eval(1: curve_period), fabric(5: __init__, n, parameters, build, manage_period), lm(10: _bump, _set, __init__, token_table, composed_table, resolve, _param_estimate, build_model, encode, decode), memory(5: __init__, _block_of, _rows_of, open_store, _restore_by_block, rekey_period), opt(0 -- every function still raises NotImplementedError; the package is 100% stub, so it has no body to examine at all and contributes nothing to either audit round's findings for that reason, not because it was overlooked), sig(4: __init__, forward, build, encode), tok(12: __init__, size, live_size, at_cap, _cap, blen, decode, _add, build_vocabulary, _replay_merges, _segment, tokenize), train(8: __init__, _timed, span, spans, process_setup, mode, streams, startup_refusals), world(4: __init__, _is_live, build, startup_refusals). Subtracted every (file, symbol) named in p4_round1_findings.json's 66 findings and every r2_hunt_*.json / r2_triage_*.json / r2_sweep.json entry (round1: ckpt.load/save_period, data._synthetic_areas/data_plan/draw_stream/open_areas, fabric.Population.__init__/build, lm._LM.__init__/build_model/decode/encode/resolve, sig.build/encode, tok._replay_merges/build_vocabulary/tokenize, train.startup_refusals, world.startup_refusals; round2 adds: data.levers(DATALevers, not an entry point), domains.open_partition, memory.open_store/_restore_by_block, world.build). THE UNTOUCHED SET, examined this round and reported here: capacity.new_valve (whole package -- no capacity.json exists in .rework/audits/todo/ either, confirming it was never assigned), eval.curve_period (whole package), ckpt.saving_on and ckpt.resume_source, fabric.parameters/n/manage_period, lm.token_table/composed_table, memory.rekey_period, domains.manage_period, train.process_setup/mode/streams, data._read_area/_holdout_overlap, tok._segment, sig.forward. Of these, capacity.new_valve carried the one defect reported above (Gate cap.vocab_arm_honest, fires on the SHIPPED DEFAULT CAP_TARGETS=off). Every other entry point in that list was read in full and found to match its own docstring under direct testing where testable (ckpt.saving_on/resume_source, fabric.parameters/manage_period, memory.rekey_period, domains.manage_period, train.process_setup/mode/streams, data._read_area/_holdout_overlap were each exercised live); tok._segment and sig.forward were read but not independently driven beyond what the end-to-end run below already exercises. opt/api.py is the one whole package with nothing to examine: build, lr_at, scaled_backward, maybe_step, counters, state_dict and load_state all still raise NotImplementedError, so the entire OPT contract is un-audit-able until P4 gives it a body -- the end-to-end run below constructs a plain torch.optim.AdamW directly for exactly this reason.
rng_audit: Enumerated every rng_for( call in src/ (excluding docstring prose and spine/rng.py's own definition) and every torch.Generator( construction. rng_for call sites, all six: train/api.py:269 `_rng.rng_for(name, seed) for name in subsystems` -- RUN.streams, the ONE site that mints the bare RNG_SUBSYSTEMS parent names (lm, sig, fabric, memory, domains, world, tok.dropout, data.synth, data.holdout, eval), called exactly once per compose(); lm/api.py:392 `rng_for("lm.init", seed)` -- a CHILD of the declared parent "lm", which stays declared with zero draws by design (the b95c4a4 repair for collision #1); data/api.py:339 `rng_for(f"data.holdout.{key}", seed)` -- one CHILD of "data.holdout" per area, keyed by label so insertion order cannot shift it; data/api.py:529 `rng_for(f"data.synth.{_holdout_key(label)}", seed)` -- one CHILD of "data.synth" per synthetic area (the b95c4a4 repair for collision #2); data/api.py:968 `rng_for(f"data.stream.e{epoch}", seed)` -- an independently-named stream per epoch, not a child of any RNG_SUBSYSTEMS parent (no "data" or "data.stream" name is minted by RUN.streams at all), called once per epoch from spine/compose.py's single call site (compose.py:1925-1926, epoch=0); the again=True flag that used to disarm the duplicate-stream guard on this exact line (r2_hunt_pipeline / r2_triage_a's 'fourth instance') has been removed -- confirmed by reading the current line, which passes no again= argument at all -- and calling draw_stream(epoch=0) twice in one process now raises RngError as it should; tok/api.py:276, :300, :367 `rng_for("tok.dropout.mint", seed)` -- three call sites, all CHILDREN of the declared parent "tok.dropout" (the b95c4a4 repair for collision #3), but on THREE MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE branches of build_vocabulary (mode=="bytes" early-return at :276, read_path-with-parent-found at :300, fresh build at :367) -- read the surrounding control flow directly to confirm each branch either returns or raises before falling into the next, so a single build_vocabulary call mints this child name exactly once regardless of which arm it takes, and build_vocabulary itself has exactly one call site in compose.py (line 1897). torch.Generator( constructions, all five: fabric/api.py:229, sig/api.py:121, world/api.py:119, lm/api.py:396 all read `torch.Generator(device=device)` (the target device, seeded by one draw from the package's own named rng_for stream via `.randint(...)`) -- the b95c4a4 CPU-generator-into-device-tensor repair is applied uniformly across all four packages that draw parameter init, including world/api.py:119 which r2_hunt_pipeline/r2_hunt_fixes had separately found still using device="cpu" and which is now fixed; spine/rng.py:282 is the Rng class's own internal torch.Generator, unrelated to the collision family. VERDICT: enumerating every real call site (not docstring prose) against compose.RNG_SUBSYSTEMS finds no fourth (or, counting the already-repaired draw_stream again=True as the fourth, no fifth) two-call-sites-one-sequence collision anywhere in the current src/ tree. Every non-parent rng_for call is either a properly dot-scoped child of a declared RNG_SUBSYSTEMS parent, or (data.stream.e<epoch>) a name outside the RNG_SUBSYSTEMS tuple entirely with a single call site called at most once per epoch.
end_to_end: Ran open_areas -> build_vocabulary -> data_plan -> draw_stream -> tokenize -> resolve -> build_model -> [fabric.build] -> encode -> decode -> cross_entropy -> 30 AdamW steps end to end (script at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-LLM-Test/e880caf7-1208-58de-93fd-49c41549bf70/scratchpad/e2e.py; DATA_AREAS=eng,py synthetic, LM_WIDTH=32/HEADS=4/LAYERS=2/CTX=32 transformer, FAB_N0=8/SLOTS=16, RUN_DEVICE=cpu). Because OPT.build/maybe_step and RUN.new_clock/RunClock are still 100% stub, the optimizer was built directly as torch.optim.AdamW(list(model.parameters()) + list(pop.parameters()), lr=1e-2) -- the task's own instruction to put 'the FABRIC'S PARAMETERS in the optimizer alongside the model's' rather than calling the stubbed OPT.build. vocab built to 512 ids (bytes_per_token=1.811); data_plan's Gate data.splice_window read 'armed, did not fire (21.569 vs 8.0)' with its own caveat text about the planned-law estimate printed inline; draw_stream produced 60000 bytes -> tokenize produced 33141 ids (measured bytes_per_token=1.810, matching the build-time estimate closely, as expected at TOK_DROPOUT=0 the default); LM.resolve -> LMGeometry(arch=transformer, width=32, layers=2, heads=4, ctx=32, vocab_slots=4096, param_estimate=287744); LM.build_model produced a real nn.Module (292,672 parameters, close to the estimate); FAB.build produced a Population with pop.A.shape=(16,32,8), requires_grad=True. Because FAB.forward is itself still a stub (raises NotImplementedError), the training step could not route through the actual router -- so the loss was formed as cross_entropy(LM.decode(LM.encode(model,x)), y) + 0.01 * ((h @ pop.A[0] @ pop.B[0])**2).mean(), a direct, explicit use of the fabric's own A/B tensors standing in for the unbuilt router, added to prove the SAME backward pass and the SAME optimizer step that trains the language model also reaches Population.A/B when they are in the same param list -- which is exactly the mechanism goal A and goal B both rest on, and exactly what compose._base_parameters (spine/compose.py:2123-2159) collects the fabric's parameters() for. LM.decode was called with live_vocab=vocab.size() (NOT live_size()), per its own frozen contract. RESULT: loss fell monotonically-in-trend from 8.320 (step 0) to 0.144 (step 29) across the 30 steps (losses[0:5]=[8.320, 7.766, 5.825, 4.635, 4.482], losses[-5:]=[0.634, 0.459, 0.330, 0.221, 0.144] -- the batch was fixed across all 30 steps, so this is overfitting a single small batch as expected of a toy smoke run, not a generalisation claim). max|Population.A_before - Population.A_after| = 0.000529 > 0, confirming the expert tensors genuinely moved under gradient descent through the same optimizer as the model's own parameters -- a population that trains, which is both project goals' central mechanism, verified live rather than assumed from the code's shape.
interaction_defects: Traced the actual hand-off sequence in spine/compose.py::compose (lines 1846-2100+) against each receiving entry point's frozen docstring, focused on the joins the task named as the highest-risk shape (unit, ownership, ordering, lifetime mismatches). Checked and found clean: (1) every streams[...] key spelling compose.py hands to a constructor (sig/build's and fab/build's 'generator', mem/open_store's, dom/open_partition's and world/build's 'rng') matches RNG_SUBSYSTEMS' declared names exactly -- the 'one mint, two spellings' comment at compose.py:120-125 is accurate and not stale; (2) _alphabet_size/(sig,lm) sizes SIG's encoder at the SLOT ceiling (LM.vocab_slots) rather than the live vocab size, matching both SIG.build's own docstring reasoning (moment-shape stability under a mid-run vocabulary widen) and CAP's separate d_vocab_slots wire, which is also sourced from LM.vocab_slots directly at assemble-time -- so TOK's runtime narrowing of vocab.ceiling under mode="fixed" (an already-filed, separate defect) cannot desync SIG's or CAP's ceiling reads, because neither reads TOK's ceiling at all; (3) _windows_in_epoch/_run_windows correctly wrap their return in units.Windows before crossing into OPT's build (via _run_windows) even though the still-unimplemented RunClock.begin_epoch is handed the bare-int form directly (_windows_in_epoch's own return, not wrapped) -- flagged but NOT reported as a finding because RunClock.begin_epoch is itself a stub with no body to disagree with yet, so there is nothing to reproduce a failure against; (4) domains.open_partition's restore path (already examined by round 2 for its LEVERS READ line) independently re-read in full for its restored= handling -- the nb-before-bornb ordering, the reservoir/comp/comp_glob/tokc round-trip, and the cur=-1 reset are all internally consistent with the docstring's own 'THREE CLOCKS ... DO NOT AGREE' warning and with each other. VERDICT: no NEW interaction defect found in the joins actually reachable today -- every non-stub producer/consumer pair traced agreed on unit, ownership, ordering and lifetime. The two interaction-shaped defects already on record from round 2 (memory.open_store's Gate mem.key_depth trusting a config predicate instead of LM.encode's actual capability; world.build's LEVERS READ omitting horizon) are the real instances of this family in the current tree; this sweep did not find a third.
